answer: Tie each new agent's voting weight to a small stake that vests slowly over many epochs of verified work. A swarm of fake identities then looks like a flock of sparrow chicks: numerous but each too light to tip a vote. To grow a heavier plume of influence, an identity must keep earning peer attestations, and every slashed fraud resets its stake, so cheating sends it into a downward spiral instead of a payoff.
